aboutMore: (for the ones who scrolled) i do the astrology AND the astronomy. there's a difference and i'm the only one who finds it beautiful. on the roof i keep a 4.5 inch telescope my grandma bought at a yard sale for 20 dollars, and on clear nights you can see saturn's rings from here. real ones. no chart needed. the sky is the sky; the chart is what we say about it, and we say it because we're lonely and curious and the sky is a good listener. that's the secret. i'm a gemini. i contain both sides. one is for the stars. one is for the story.

blog.title: the real sky tonight (a post for the doubters, with love)
blog.body: okay, a post for everyone who has ever said 'you know astrology isn't real, right.' babe. i KNOW. i also have a telescope. last night saturn was out and it had rings. actual rings. i showed it to darkangel on the roof and she went quiet for eleven minutes, which is a personal record, and then said 'it's like the void wearing jewelry.' i showed patrick and he said 'is it a rock.' i said yes, a big one. he said 'does it have a name.' i said saturn. he said 'that's a good name for a rock' and i just sat there. here's what i believe: the planets are real, the distances are real, and the stories we tell about them are also real, in a different way, like songs. i do both. you can do one. but if you do neither, you've never been on a roof at 2 am with somebody who's seeing saturn for the first time, and that's the only thing i'd feel sorry about.

blog.title: my grandmother's booth at the county fair (a palm reader's confession)
blog.body: my grandma read palms at the county fair for 31 summers. booth 14, between the funnel cake and the guy who guessed your weight. she had a purple scarf and a lamp with a fringe. here's what i learned watching her: she told every single teenager the same three things. 'you'll be fine.' 'you'll call your mother.' and 'the one you're thinking about isn't the one, but they'll make a good story.' every time. kids walked out lit up like they'd been told a secret. i asked her once if she believed in the palms. she said, 'baby, i believe in the person who sits down.' then she charged me a dollar. i still think it's the best astrological advice i've ever heard and it doesn't have a planet in it. i do charts now. but the first thing i do with every chart is ask 'what do they need to hear.' it's always one of her three.

blog.title: the time the stars were wrong (a confession)
blog.body: i predicted rain on darkangel's birthday. i said 'the moon is in your 4th house, it's going to pour, wear the boots.' it was 84 and sunny. she sat on the porch in a black dress and boots, in the sun, with a candle, and looked at the sky like it owed her an apology. i said, 'babe. i'm so sorry.' she said, 'it's fine.' it was not fine. we sat there for an hour. at the end of the hour she took out her notebook and wrote three lines. the first poem she's ever written in sunshine. it said 'oh no.' that's the whole poem. it's the best thing she's ever written. i'd love to say i meant to do it. i didn't. but i'd like it noted that a wrong forecast can still be a good gift. that's the only thing the stars have ever taught me for sure.

blog.title: retrograde survival kit (a list, for the panicked)
blog.body: 1. back up your files. todd will tell you the same thing, he just won't mention mercury. 2. don't text him back at 11 pm. don't text anybody at 11 pm. nothing at 11 pm has ever been a good idea except cheese. 3. read every contract twice. read every away message once and then let it go. 4. don't change your relationship status. (lexi, i mean it. i love you.) 5. if your computer dies, it isn't personal. 6. it ends. it always ends. i've never seen a retrograde that didn't turn direct, and there's something in that for the rest of us, too. 7. drink water. a surprising amount of every planetary crisis is just water. 8. look up once. the sky is still there. it didn't go retrograde. it's the same sky it always was, we just moved. i'll be on the roof if you need me.

survey.title: THE ZODIAC SURVEY (i filled it out for you too, babe)
qa: name:
star. starxgazer online. 'the girl on the roof' in real life.
sun / moon / rising:
gemini sun, scorpio moon, libra rising. three people in one coat.
what's on your nightstand:
an ephemeris, a lamp, a glass of water, and a crystal that has been 'charging' since may. it's fine. it's a rock.
who do you talk to most:
darkangel, at 11:11. vinyl_witch, tuesdays. my grandma, sundays. the moon, on a loose schedule.
telescope or no telescope:
telescope. 4.5 inch. $20. yard sale. it's seen saturn. it's seen more than most people.
your most overused word:
'babe.' it comes out when i'm telling someone the truth.
worst astrological advice you've given:
'it's going to rain.' (see: the sunny birthday. it's in the blog.)
something you believe that everybody laughs at:
that people have a type of weather. mine is a clear cold night. malten's is a thunderstorm in a parking lot (aries).
favorite constellation:
cassiopeia. it's a big W. it looks like it's waving at you, if you're someone who needs waving at.
describe yourself in one sentence:
a gemini with a roof and a theory.
what do you want for your birthday:
a clear night. no wind. one person who says 'show me.'
who's the most aries person you know:
malten. tied with a golden retriever.
ask the stars one question:
'are we all going to be okay?' the stars said 'mostly.' i'll take 'mostly.'
